memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Present with this bread seven male lambs, each a year old and without
defect, one young bull and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to
the LORD, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings - a
food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD. Then sacrifice one male
goat for a sin offering and two lambs, each a year old, for a
fellowship offering'" - Lev 23:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
. A sin offering, because even in celebration Israel needed
atonement. Fellowship offerings, which were shared and eaten together
in joy.

Dear reader, that combination is instructive. Even at their most
joyful festival, God's people did not forget they were sinners needing
covering. And even while acknowledging sin, they still feasted.

Both belong in Christian worship. We come honestly, aware of our need.
And we come joyfully, because that need has been met in Christ. Hebrews
tells us Jesus offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, then sat
down at the right hand of God (Heb 10:12). The sin offering is
finished. The feast continues.

Some believers are all sorrow and no joy. Others are all celebration
and no honesty. Scripture holds them together.

Come to God today aware of your need and glad in His grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my worship honest about sin and still full of joy?
2. Do I lean too far toward guilt or toward casual celebration?
3. Is my giving to God generous or merely token?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Jesus' one sacrifice has dealt with my sin
completely. Let me worship You honestly and joyfully at the same time.
Amen.
